chunks: One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Muḥammad ibn ṬalḈah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Whichever servant has a handsome appearance along with an untainted position, then he humbles himself before Allah, he will be among the special [chosen] ones of Allah.'
He (the narrator) said, 'I asked, What is [the meaning of] an untainted position?' He replied, 'He should not have been sullied by debauchery.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a servant to have an untainted position and be among the special chosen ones of Allah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the criteria for divine favor are linked to the harmony of physical beauty, moral integrity, and humility. The specific condition of 'a place that does not disfigure him' is interpreted by scholars as freedom from major sexual sins, ensuring that outward beauty is not marred by inner corruption. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the unity of appearance and character in achieving spiritual excellence.
